CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left arm pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is an elderly male presenting with left arm pain that began approximately two weeks ago. He reports waking up around 2:00 AM with severe pain in the arm. Applied ice which provided some relief. The pain pattern initially occurred nightly, lasting until approximately 4-5 AM when it would ease, though this happened repeatedly over several nights. He was previously evaluated by another physician who suspected a pinched nerve. Pain starts in the hand and radiates down the entire arm. Patient reports associated weakness in the hand, particularly with gripping. He notes a prior finger injury that does not function properly. Pain tends to occur at night, and if present at night, typically continues to some degree the following day. Recently, neck pain has improved over the last couple of nights, but hand symptoms persist. Patient was started on numbing medicine, a neck medication, and gabapentin, which have provided some benefit. Denies neck or head movement worsening symptoms. Denies shoulder discomfort.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Weakness in left hand and grip strength. Radiating pain down left arm from hand. Denies neck movement exacerbating symptoms. Denies shoulder pain with movement.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Neuropathy (service-connected, 1% disability rating)
Cervical spine arthritis with disc degeneration
Prior lower back imaging

MEDICATIONS
Gabapentin (dosage uncertain, managed by companion)
Numbing medicine
Neck medication
Eliquis

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

Veteran with service-connected disability
Uses wheelchair

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Elderly white male in wheelchair, no apparent distress. Cervical spine non-tender. Mildly restricted cervical extension. Right and left lateral rotation symmetric with mild lateral neck pain but no radicular pain. Spurling's maneuver benign. Bilateral hand grip strength intact. Able to maintain arm rigidity against resistance. Sensation intact bilaterally. Reflexes: 1+ bilateral biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis, all negative. Gait not assessed. Lower extremities not fully assessed.

RESULTS
Cervical x-ray (6421): Significant disc degeneration at C5-C6, with lower extent involvement at C4-C5 and C3-C4. Significant facet arthropathy at C6-C7. C7-T1 difficult to visualize. MRI of cervical spine ordered, pending scheduling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left upper extremity neuropathy suspicious for cervical radiculopathy with possible contribution of peripheral neuropathy.
2. Neck pain in setting of cervical arthritis and disc degeneration.

Plan: Suspect flare of cervical radiculopathy. Cervical MRI ordered to determine exact location of nerve compression. Tentatively plan left C7-T1 epidural injection with exact location to be determined by MRI results. Continue home exercise program. Continue gabapentin twice daily. Follow up after epidural injection to assess symptom relief. Patient denies use of blood thinners.
